headline.text: MV Arctic Fern (VG-1088) is the vessel most likely to miss its Rotterdam berth window. Its revised ETA is already 23 h after the window closes. MV Kestrel Bay (VG-1091) and MV Celtic Dawn (VG-1102) are lower-risk watch items. The other three show no slip.

interpretation.text: "Next week" is Mon 2026-11-02 to Sun 2026-11-08, using port-local dates and revised ETA. Six voyages are due at NLRTM in that range. Port-wide congestion is context only.

confirmed_facts.text: MV Arctic Fern (VG-1088, from SGSIN) is Delayed. Its revised ETA is 2026-11-04T14:00Z, against a berth window that closes 2026-11-03T15:00Z. The ETA slipped 33 h, and the recorded delay is 33 h.
A Confirmed incident, hull fouling / speed loss (INC-221, reported by the technical manager), attributes 33 h to VG-1088. That equals the recorded delay, so the delay is fully explained.

The other four voyages show zero ETA slip and 10 h to spare before their windows close: Northern Lark VG-1097, Amber Coast VG-1099, Rio Verde VG-1095 and, on the schedule data alone, Kestrel Bay VG-1091 and Celtic Dawn VG-1102. Rio Verde has not yet departed and is scheduled to leave 2026-10-27.

unverified_reports.text: The crew of Kestrel Bay (VG-1091) reported that the no.2 aux engine tripped twice and the vessel is running on no.1 and no.3. The incident is INC-224, status Reported, with no attributed delay. The crew said it "may need parts in Rotterdam" and "no speed loss so far". All of this is unverified.
The master of Celtic Dawn (VG-1102) reported a main engine fuel pump fault (INC-219, status Reported). The attributed delay is unknown, which is not the same as zero.

inferences.text: Arctic Fern will very likely miss its window. It would arrive about 23 h after the window closes, and the window is on 3 Nov. This depends on the ETA holding and on the speed loss not worsening. Rotterdam's high congestion could add a further wait once it arrives, but that is port-wide and not specific to this vessel.
inferences.based_on: Vessel evidence: the revised ETA is past the window end and a Confirmed hull-fouling incident explains the slip. Port context: congestion level High, average wait 36 h on 2026-10-26.

inferences.text: Kestrel Bay is the next most at risk. The 10 h margin is small against Rotterdam's 36 h average wait, and a possible unverified engine fault and parts need could cause delay. Celtic Dawn is a lower-tier watch item because of its unverified fuel pump fault. Its ETA has not moved.
inferences.based_on: Unverified incident reports on those vessels, a small schedule margin, and port-wide congestion. This is a judgement, not a recorded delay.

data_gaps.text: Congestion data ends 2026-10-26, so conditions for 2–8 Nov are unknown. messages/extra (45 files) was not loaded, so further reports may be missing.

recommended_checks.text: Ask the Nordwave Marine technical manager whether a new berth window at Rotterdam has been requested for Arctic Fern. The ETA of 4 Nov is after the 3 Nov window closes. Also check the knock-on effect on bookings.

Get the Kestrel Bay master or technical manager to confirm the auxiliary engine status and whether parts are needed at Rotterdam. Also ask Celtic Dawn's master for the fuel pump fault's impact on speed and ETA.
